findings_addressed.oracle: The _add_call_info processor in src/intellicrack/core/logging.py (lines 234-236) records module as the source filename stem and function as frame.f_code.co_name. The only callers of logger.info/warning in that test function are in test_reader_parses_real_structlog_records inside test_realcov_15_tail_reader_real_logs.py, so the expected values are determined independently from the call site.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/core/logging.py line 234, change `event_dict["module"] = frame.f_code.co_filename.rsplit("\\", 1)[-1].rsplit("/", 1)[-1].replace(".py", "")` to `event_dict["module"] = "unknown"` — the assertion `assert alpha["module"] == "test_realcov_15_tail_reader_real_logs"` would then fail.

notes: Replaced lines 87-88 (bare truthiness `assert str(alpha['module'])` and `assert str(alpha['function'])`) with exact equality assertions against the known call-site values: module must equal the test filename stem 'test_realcov_15_tail_reader_real_logs' and function must equal the test function name 'test_reader_parses_real_structlog_records'. These values are independently derivable from the source location of the logger.info call and from knowledge of how _add_call_info extracts frame information. A no-op implementation that writes placeholder strings such as 'unknown' now fails the gate.
